paragraphs: Following a decisive defeat in the US midterm elections, Donald Trump and the Republican Party have lost control of both houses of Congress to the Democrats. The results have sparked intense disputes within both major parties.

Among Republicans, Vice President JD Vance has attributed the electoral losses to the unpopular war with Iran, which created a visible rift with the president. At the same time, Donald Trump has sent mixed signals regarding his policy direction: while publicly acknowledging that his strict immigration enforcement went too far, he appointed Stephen Miller, the architect of those policies, as White House Chief of Staff. On the Democratic side, progressives and moderates are competing to shape the party’s future legislative agenda.

Political analysts warn that despite the significant shift in congressional control, deep ideological divisions and the president’s veto power will likely lead to continued political gridlock in Washington rather than major policy changes.

words.d: a disagreement, argument, or debate between people, parties, or groups
a serious break in friendly relations between people or groups
a situation where no progress can be made because of strong disagreement or opposing forces

paragraphs: The Democratic Party won big in the US midterm elections and took control of both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republican Party.

This defeat caused strong arguments inside both parties. Vice President JD Vance blamed the election loss on the war with Iran, and disagreed directly with Trump. At the same time, Trump said his strict immigration rules went too far, but he still chose the creator of those rules to lead his White House team. Meanwhile, Democrats are fighting over their plans, as its members want different things.

Experts say that even with new Democratic leaders in Congress, it will be hard to pass major new laws because the president can still block them, which may lead to more political delays in Washington.

words.d: the loss of a contest, game, election, or battle
to say or think that someone or something is responsible for something bad that happened

paragraphs: The Democrats win a big election in the US. They now control Congress. President Donald Trump and his team lose many votes.

Now, people in both political parties are fighting about what to do next. Vice President JD Vance says that the war with Iran is a bad idea. Many people do not like Trump anymore because of that. Trump said that his immigration rules are too hard. But he still puts his immigration leader in a top job. At the same time, Democrats are trying to agree on new plans for the country.
Experts think that it will still be very hard for leaders in Washington to pass new laws and help people quickly.
